models.name: Renault Clio III 1.2 16V
facts: D4F, 1,149 cc petrol, four cylinders, 16 valves, about 75 PS
models.source: Wikipedia, 'Renault Clio' (Clio III) and 'Renault D engine' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_D_engine

models.name: Renault Clio III 1.2 TCe 100
facts: D4FT, 1,149 cc turbocharged petrol, 16 valves, about 100 PS
models.source: Wikipedia, 'Renault D engine' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_D_engine

models.name: Renault Clio III 1.5 dCi
facts: K9K, 1,461 cc common-rail turbodiesel, 8 valves, about 75 or 88 PS in the 2012 UK range
Later versions carry a diesel particulate filter
models.source: Wikipedia, 'Renault K engine' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_K_engine

models.name: Renault Clio III Renaultsport 200
facts: F4R, 1,998 cc petrol, 16 valves, about 200 PS
models.source: Wikipedia, 'Renault Clio' (Clio Renault Sport) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_Clio

models.name: Renault Clio in 2012: which generation
facts: A car first registered in the UK in 2012 is almost always a Clio III phase 2 (facelifted in 2009)
Shown at the Paris Motor Show in September 2012; UK deliveries began around the turn of 2013
3- and 5-door hatchback, and the Sport Tourer estate
models.source: Wikipedia, 'Renault Clio' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_Clio

models.name: Renault Clio III timing belt
facts: Every UK engine of the period (D4F, D4FT, K9K, F4R) uses a toothed timing belt
Renault's UK schedules give roughly 72,000 miles or 5–6 years depending on engine and year; many garages advise doing it sooner
Tensioner and idler, and the water pump where the belt drives it
models.source: Renault UK service schedule as summarised by owners' clubs (clio.net forums) and Wikipedia's engine pages; confirm in the car's service book

models.name: Renault Clio III oil and service
facts: Petrol: an oil meeting Renault RN0700, typically 5W-30 or 5W-40. Diesel with a particulate filter: RN0720
About 4 to 5 litres with filter, depending on engine; check the dipstick, not the litres
Annual, with a mileage limit of about 12,000–18,000 miles by engine
models.source: Renault owner's handbook guidance as quoted by major UK oil makers' look-up tools (e.g. Castrol, Comma); confirm for the exact engine

models.name: Renault Clio III coolant and brake fluid
facts: Renault Glaceol RX Type D or an equivalent long-life coolant
models.source: Renault owner's handbook guidance as quoted by UK parts retailers' fluid look-ups; confirm in the handbook

models.name: Renault Clio III tyre sizes
facts: On a label inside the driver's door
models.source: UK tyre retailers' size look-ups by model (e.g. Kwik Fit, Black Circles); confirm on the tyre sidewall

models.name: Renault Clio III bulbs
facts: H7 dipped and H1 main beam on most halogen lamps (check before buying)
P21/5W stop and tail, P21W reverse and fog
models.source: UK bulb retailers' vehicle look-ups (e.g. Ring, Halfords); confirm against the old bulb

models.name: Renault Clio III common known issues
facts: Coil packs on the 1.2 16V failing, giving a misfire
Card reader and body computer faults leading to no start
EGR, injector and turbo faults on the 1.5 dCi, and DPF blockage on short trips
Blower resistor failure, fan only on top speed
Front anti-roll bar links and lower arm bushes knocking
models.source: Honest John and What Car? used Clio III reviews, and owners' clubs; patterns, not certainties

models.name: BMW E30 316i
facts: M40B16, 1,596 cc four-cylinder petrol, single overhead cam, about 100 PS
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW M40' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_M40

models.name: BMW E30 318i
facts: M40B18, 1,796 cc four-cylinder petrol, single overhead cam, about 115 PS
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW M40' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_M40

models.name: BMW E30 320i
facts: M20B20, 1,990 cc straight-six petrol, single overhead cam, about 129 PS
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW M20' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_M20

models.name: BMW E30 325i
facts: M20B25, 2,494 cc straight-six petrol, single overhead cam, about 171 PS with a catalyst-free tune
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW M20' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_M20

models.name: BMW E30 saloon in 1989–90
facts: E30, built 1982–1994; the facelift of 1987 brought plastic bumpers and new rear lamps
316i and 318i with the M40 four, 320i and 325i with the M20 six
Rear-wheel drive; a 325i Touring and the M3 were other bodies of the same family
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW 3 Series (E30)' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_3_Series_(E30)

models.name: BMW E30 timing belt
facts: Both the M40 and M20 engines use a toothed timing belt, and both are interference engines
Enthusiast clubs advise about every 4 years or 40,000–60,000 miles, with a new tensioner
Worn camshaft lobes and rocker arms are worth checking with the cover off
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW M20' and 'BMW M40', and the BMW Car Club GB E30 register

models.name: BMW E30 oil and service
facts: A good 10W-40 or 15W-40 suits these engines' age
About 4 litres (M40) or 4.3 litres (M20) with filter; check the dipstick
The dashboard Service Interval Indicator lights call for an Oil Service or an Inspection, roughly every 7,500–15,000 miles by how the car is driven
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW 3 Series (E30)', and owners' clubs' maintenance guides; confirm in the service book

models.name: BMW E30 coolant and brake fluid
facts: Blue BMW-type ethylene glycol antifreeze mixed 50:50 with water
The plastic expansion tank, thermostat housing and viscous fan clutch age badly
models.source: Owners' clubs' maintenance guides (BMW Car Club GB, r3vlimited forum)

models.name: BMW E30 tyre sizes
facts: 175/70 R14 on steel or alloy wheels
195/65 R14, or 205/55 R15 on later sports alloys
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW 3 Series (E30)', and UK tyre retailers' size look-ups

models.name: BMW E30 bulbs
facts: Four round lamps with H1 bulbs on most UK facelift cars (some use H4 in the outer lamps; check before buying)
P21/5W stop and tail, P21W reverse
models.source: UK bulb retailers' vehicle look-ups and owners' clubs; confirm against the old bulb

models.name: BMW E30 common known issues
facts: Sills, jacking points, rear arches, the front valance, the battery tray and the floor under blocked sunroof drains
Timing belts and tensioners left too long; M40 camshaft wear; M20 head cracks after overheating
Rear subframe and trailing arm bushes, front control arm bushes
Odometer gears that crack and stop the mileage
models.source: Wikipedia, 'BMW 3 Series (E30)', and classic car buying guides (e.g. Classic Cars for Sale, Practical Classics)
